Why is a min-token floor important when using semantic chunking?
options: Without a floor, semantic chunking can produce tiny 40-token fragments that hurt retrieval

questions.q: What does 'late chunking' do differently from traditional chunking?
options: Embeds the whole document at the token level first, then pools token embeddings into chunk vectors to preserve cross-chunk context

questions.q: What is the goal of coreference resolution?
options: Cluster all mentions (named, nominal, pronominal) that refer to the same real-world entity

questions.q: Which type of expression is a 'nominal' mention?
options: A noun phrase such as 'the CEO' or 'the company'

questions.q: What is the modern (Lee et al., 2017) coref architecture?
options: End-to-end span-based: enumerate spans, score mentions, then score antecedent probabilities and cluster greedily

questions.q: What does CoNLL F1 average?
options: MUC, B-cubed, and CEAF-phi4 F1 scores

questions.q: What is bridging anaphora?
options: An implicit reference like 'the wheels' implying the wheels of a previously mentioned car

questions.q: Why is LLM-only coref unreliable on long documents?
options: Single-call LLMs over-merge or silently drop mentions across 50+ paragraphs; require sliding-window plus merge

questions.q: Why merge coref clusters into NER results before downstream tasks?
options: So downstream tasks see one entity per cluster rather than one per surface mention, dramatically improving coverage

questions.q: Why are hard-coded gender rules a fragility in coref systems?
options: They break on non-binary referents, organizations, and animals; learned scoring is more robust

questions.q: What does entity linking add on top of NER?
options: It maps each detected mention to a unique entry in a knowledge base (Wikidata, Wikipedia, or a domain KB)

questions.q: What are the two main subtasks in entity linking?
options: Candidate generation (shortlist of plausible KB entries) and disambiguation (pick the right one given context)

questions.q: Why must mention recall be reported alongside disambiguation accuracy?
options: Disambiguation cannot recover from missing candidates; the pipeline is bounded by candidate-generation recall
Mention recall is mandatory by GDPR

questions.q: How does GENRE perform entity linking?
options: Decodes the entity's canonical name token-by-token under constrained decoding over a trie of valid KB ids

questions.q: What is NIL handling in entity linking?
options: Predicting a 'not in KB' label when no candidate is a real match (emerging entities, obscure people)

questions.q: Why does popularity bias hurt entity linking in specialized domains?
options: Models trained on web data over-predict frequent entities (e.g. basketball Jordan over the ML researcher Michael I. Jordan)
It biases toward older entities only

questions.q: What is a safe LLM-EL pattern in 2026?
options: Provide a candidate list and use constrained JSON output that the LLM can only choose from valid KB ids

questions.q: Why must NER mention boundaries be exact for entity linking to work?
options: Boundary errors propagate: 'Bank of America' clipped to 'Bank' surfaces wrong candidates and tanks EL recall
Boundary precision only affects NER metrics, not entity-linking candidate quality

questions.q: What is the atomic unit of a knowledge graph?
What does AEVS stand for in 2026 relation extraction?
options: Anchor-Extraction-Verification-Supplement: anchor spans, extract triples, verify against source, supplement coverage

questions.q: Why must each triple carry source provenance (doc id + span)?
options: Provenance lets you audit triples and reject hallucinations whose spans do not match the source text

questions.q: What does canonicalization of relations do?
options: Maps surface verb phrases (e.g. 'was born in', 'is a native of') onto a fixed property id so the graph is queryable

questions.q: Why does relation extraction usually need coreference resolution first?
options: Pronouns like 'he founded Apple' must be resolved to a named entity before triple extraction

questions.q: Which choice trades open IE recall for graph queryability?
options: Mapping open-IE relations onto a closed ontology (e.g. Wikidata properties) before merging into the KG

questions.q: Why do many production KGs use temporal qualifiers (start/end time)?
options: Many relations are time-bounded (employer, spouse, role); qualifiers prevent 'forever true' claims that go stale

questions.q: What is REBEL?
options: A seq2seq relation extractor that outputs triples already in Wikidata property ids

questions.q: Why are Exact Match and token-F1 insufficient for evaluating modern LLM outputs?
options: They miss semantic equivalence; 'June 29th, 2007' vs 'June 29, 2007' scores 0 EM despite being correct

questions.q: What does the RAGAS faithfulness metric measure?
options: Whether each claim in the answer is entailed by the retrieved context, via NLI

questions.q: Why is judge-model calibration against human labels required before trusting scores?
options: If Spearman correlation between judge and human labels is too low (e.g. below 0.7), the score is noise rather than signal

questions.q: What is self-evaluation bias in LLM-as-judge setups?
options: Judges run faster on cached outputs
Using the same LLM family to generate and judge inflates scores by 10-20% versus an independent judge

questions.q: What does G-Eval specifically add over a naive 'score 0-1' prompt?
options: An explicit chain-of-thought rubric with named evaluation steps, which yields more stable scores

questions.q: Why is reporting only the aggregate mean score dangerous?
options: An 0.85 mean can hide 5% catastrophic failures; always inspect the bottom quantile

questions.q: Why pin the judge model + version in CI?
options: Upgrading the judge changes every metric; longitudinal comparison breaks without a frozen judge

questions.q: Where does DeepEval fit relative to RAGAS?
options: DeepEval is pytest-for-LLMs (CI gates, G-Eval, hallucination metrics); RAGAS specializes in reference-free RAG monitoring

questions.q: What does the original NIAH benchmark measure?
options: Whether the model can retrieve a planted fact at controlled depths across a long context

questions.q: Why is the advertised context window often very different from the usable context?
options: Attention degrades with length and task; spec-sheet maximums rarely hold under multi-hop or reasoning loads

questions.q: What does RULER add over NIAH?
options: Thirteen task types across retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, and QA at multiple context lengths

questions.q: What is the 'lost in the middle' effect?
options: Models under-attend to content placed in the middle of long inputs; depth=0.5 often performs worse than depth=0 or 1

questions.q: Why must NIAH-only evaluation be supplemented with multi-hop tests?
options: Frontier models can ace single-needle retrieval but still fail multi-hop variable-tracing or aggregation tasks
NIAH cannot run on long context

questions.q: What does NoLiMa stress?
options: Needles that share no literal tokens with the query, so retrieval requires a semantic reasoning step

questions.q: What two numbers should a long-context spec sheet report?
options: Effective retrieval length (e.g. 90% NIAH pass) and effective reasoning length (e.g. 70% multi-hop pass)

questions.q: Why measure time-to-first-token at long context lengths?
options: 1M-token prefills can take tens of seconds; accuracy alone hides product-impacting latency

questions.q: What does dialogue state tracking maintain across turns?
options: A slot-value dictionary representing the user's current goal, updated after every turn

questions.q: What does Joint Goal Accuracy (JGA) measure?
options: Fraction of turns where every slot is exactly correct (all-or-nothing)

questions.q: Why does regenerating the whole state from history each turn handle user corrections naturally?
options: Reading the full history lets the model re-derive the final state including 'actually...' corrections without explicit rollback logic

questions.q: Which 2026 pattern gives a guaranteed-valid slot dict in 5 lines of code?
options: LLM + Instructor + Pydantic schema with constrained or validated output

questions.q: Why version your DST schema?
options: Adding new slots post-hoc invalidates older training data and breaks longitudinal evaluation

questions.q: Why must DST for compliance-sensitive domains include a rule-based check alongside LLM extraction?
options: LLM-only DST can mis-extract destructive parameters (amount, account, date); a rules layer enforces deterministic constraints

questions.q: What is the cost concern with regenerating state on every turn via LLM?
options: Re-reading the full history each turn yields O(n^2) total token usage; cap or summarize older turns

questions.q: Why are explicit confirmation flows required before destructive backend actions?
options: Even good DST has nonzero slot-error rates; a deterministic confirmation prevents wrong-account or wrong-amount actions
